title: Triage and rotate historical credentials flagged by Gitleaks
description: A redacted full-history Gitleaks scan found 36 pre-existing findings across old fixtures, test tokens, Sentry property files, and Linear configuration. The current homelab migration diff is clean. Credential values were not inspected or printed.
design: Classify every finding as synthetic, false positive, expired, or live using redacted identifiers only. Revoke or rotate any credential that may have been valid, preserve provider ownership evidence, and decide whether history rewrite is warranted without disrupting shared clones.
acceptance_criteria: All 36 findings are dispositioned; every possibly live credential is proven revoked or rotated; current provider custody uses replacement values; the working migration diff remains Gitleaks-clean; any history remediation has an approved coordination plan.

title: Resolve production dependency advisories before homelab deployment
description: Current production audits after narrow safe upgrades report 2 critical and 70 high findings in the root workspace, 7 high in the Rails JS bundle, and 2 high in HTML-to-image. The web runtime still contains tar 6.2.0 through re2/metascraper, Next 14.2.35 has high advisories patched only in supported 15.5.x or newer lines, and the Sanity toolchain's decompress advisory names an unpublished patched release. Do not hide these with unsafe major-version overrides.
design: Audit the actual pruned/runtime dependency graphs and container SBOMs. Upgrade or replace vulnerable runtime paths with compatibility tests; classify build-only/non-runtime paths separately. Do not accept repo-wide counts as proof of image exposure, and do not force incompatible transitive majors without build/runtime evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Each deployable image has an SBOM-scoped advisory report with zero applicable critical/high findings or an explicit reviewed mitigation; Next runs on a supported patched line; frozen installs, tests, and all runtime builds pass.
notes: 2026-08-12: Restored @shopify/react-shortcuts and ShortcutProvider at user request; no shortcut behavior change remains. Tiptap Pro migration remains deferred pending dedicated compatibility confirmation. uuid@9 and Playwright 1.43 remain pending deliberate runtime/test migration work. No dependency source or lockfile changes are retained from this exploratory pass.

title: Run post-cutover UAT, monitoring, and rollback soak
description: Observe the homelab deployment through the agreed rollback window and complete human UAT across desktop/mobile browser, uploads, notes, search, notifications, integrations, MCP, jobs, and recovery monitoring.
design: Keep polo-apps infrastructure available but non-authoritative. Track errors, latency, queue depth, storage growth, backup success, tunnel availability, and power/network incidents. Treat missing telemetry as unavailable, not healthy.
acceptance_criteria: Human UAT is explicitly accepted; no unresolved severity-one migration defects remain; backups continue succeeding; operational metrics meet agreed thresholds for the full soak period; rollback is still executable.

title: Execute production cutover to camp.tokdio.com
description: During an approved maintenance window, quiesce writes, migrate final authoritative data, switch background-worker custody, apply DNS/Cloudflare and provider changes, and make camp.tokdio.com canonical.
design: No schema or feature release is bundled with the infrastructure migration. Preserve old services and data unchanged for rollback. Capture exact revisions, timestamps, counts, and external probes throughout.
acceptance_criteria: The tokdio hostname family serves the authoritative homelab stack; source/target data reconciles; exactly one worker/scheduler fleet is active; external authenticated and provider validations pass; rollback remains available.

title: Rehearse cutover, rollback, and authenticated acceptance
description: Run a production-shaped cutover rehearsal covering write quiescence, final database/object delta, search validation, worker handoff, Cloudflare routing, provider callbacks, authenticated browser flows, and rollback.
design: Only one Sidekiq scheduler/worker fleet may be active. Test from outside the LAN and prove Cloudflare edge-to-origin routing, not just container health. Include explicit decision points and abort thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: The complete sequence and rollback finish within agreed RTO; authenticated browser, upload/media, notes sync, jobs, email, provider, MCP, and webhook checks pass; residual risks and human approvals are explicit.

title: Build and rehearse production data migration
description: Create repeatable migration procedures for MySQL, Redis/Sidekiq state, Elasticsearch, and S3 objects. Perform at least one full restore-based rehearsal using production-shaped snapshots and calculate final outage duration.
design: Prefer native dump/restore or replication tools with checksums and resumability. Elasticsearch may be rebuilt from MySQL only if completeness and duration are proven. Object transfer must preserve keys, content types, metadata, and application-visible URLs.
acceptance_criteria: Rehearsal completes without touching authoritative production data; source/target counts and checksums reconcile; the exact final delta/quiescence procedure, timings, and rollback boundary are documented.

title: Implement and prove backup and disaster recovery
description: Implement scheduled, encrypted backups for MySQL, Redis where required for recovery, Elasticsearch snapshots, and object storage; store copies on starkdrive and one failure-independent destination. Document retention, monitoring, and recovery procedures.
design: A backup is not accepted until restored into isolated services and validated at the application/data level. VM snapshots complement but do not replace logical/database and object backups.
acceptance_criteria: A timed restore drill reconstructs all authoritative state from backups, verifies row/index/object counts and sampled content, records achieved RPO/RTO, and raises an alert for a deliberately failed backup.

title: Design and declare the homelab production platform
description: Define the Odin container topology, networks, persistent volumes, resource limits, health checks, secret injection, Kamal proxy routing, Forge build path, Heimdall Cloudflare ingress, starkdrive backup destinations, monitoring, alerting, and power/network failure behavior.
design: Prefer declared configuration in the Campsite and homelab repositories. Keep application traffic private behind Cloudflare Tunnel; expose no database/cache/search/storage admin ports publicly. Separate backup credentials from runtime credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed declared-state design covers deployment, storage, networking, secrets, observability, capacity, backup paths, failure modes, and rollback; configuration validates without mutating production.
notes:
Declared-state design added at docs/deployment/homelab-production.md.

Reviewed coverage:
- Deployment: separate Kamal destination configs for each application image; immutable Git-revision tags; Forge preferred builder with Odin fallback.
- Placement/capacity: Odin app and durable-data ceilings total 4.6 GiB; Shuri Elasticsearch capped at 2 GiB/1 GiB heap; provisioning disk safety gate.
- Networking: Heimdall Cloudflare Tunnel to Odin Kamal proxy; no public stateful admin ports; authenticated Odin-to-Shuri search path required.
- Storage: local live volumes; starkdrive backup-only because the current NFS mount is soft.
- Secrets: runtime, migration, backup, and operator custody separated; values excluded from Git/config.
- Observability: Beszel plus resource, service, synthetic-path, queue, search, and backup-age checks.
- Recovery: explicit RPO/RTO/maintenance/rollback objectives and failure-mode matrix.
- Rollback: per-runtime immutable-image rollback plus whole-stack data/DNS/provider rollback custody.

Validation:
- kamal config -d campsite-shadow rendered successfully and confirmed Odin application plus Shuri accessory host topology.
- git diff --check passed.
- No host, DNS, Cloudflare, provider, or production mutation was performed.

Deferred to dependent implementation/provisioning Beads:
- Production runtime images/configs and missing Rails/sync liveness endpoints.
- Authenticated/firewalled Odin-to-Shuri Elasticsearch path.
- Provider data-size measurement after Fly/provider authentication.
- Backup credentials, schedules, and successful restore evidence.
close_reason: Reviewed homelab production declared-state design covers platform, capacity, networking, storage, secrets, observability, backups, failure modes, and rollback; shadow Kamal config validates read-only.

title: Audit live Campsite topology, data ownership, and homelab capacity
description: Inventory exact deployed revisions, runtime processes, database engine/version/size, Redis persistence and queues, Elasticsearch indexes, object count/bytes, provider callbacks, secrets custody, traffic, and backup state. Live-check Odin, Forge, Heimdall, starkdrive, Cloudflare Tunnel, power/network resilience, and available CPU/RAM/disk.
design: Read-only evidence pass. Record secrets by name and custody only, never values. Establish RPO, RTO, maintenance-window, rollback-window, and capacity headroom before provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: A current evidence-backed inventory identifies every production component and authoritative data source; Odin and storage capacity are measured live; RPO/RTO and migration maintenance constraints are explicit; unknowns remain marked unavailable rather than assumed.
notes:
Live audit completed 2026-08-11.

CURRENT PRODUCTION:
- Web camp.polo-apps.com is on Vercel and redirects / to /up/posts.
- API and auth are Rails endpoints behind Cloudflare/Caddy.
- Sync, styled-text, and HTML-to-image resolve directly to legacy host 51.91.240.88.
- Legacy host has 31 GiB RAM with 12 GiB available, but root disk is 94 percent used with 7.2 GiB free. Exact helper image revisions were recorded live.
- Stateful services identified: primary and replica MySQL via DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_REPLICA_URL; separate Redis URLs for Sidekiq and cache; Elasticsearch; S3-compatible object storage; plus Vercel and external integrations.
- Fly CLI has no authenticated token. Current Fly revisions, MySQL and Redis sizes, Elasticsearch data size, and object count and bytes are UNAVAILABLE until operator authentication. No values were inferred.

APPLICATION CUSTODY:
- Production search URL is currently hardcoded to loopback port 9300.
- Sidekiq concurrency is 5 and production schedules outbound jobs.
- Object storage uses configurable endpoint, region, bucket, access key, secret, and path-style settings.
- External custody includes Pusher, Slack, Figma, Linear, 100ms, Postmark/SMTP, Google and GitHub OAuth, web push, Imgix, Cloudflare CDN, Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic/Plain, Vercel, Sentry, and Axiom.

HOMELAB CAPACITY AND PLACEMENT:
- Asgard host: 17.0 GB total, about 1.64 GB free with Odin, Heimdall, Hermes, and Plex running.
- Odin: 8 GiB/3 vCPU, 6.3 GiB available, 79 GB root free. Good app-runtime target.
- Heimdall: 4 GiB/1 vCPU, 1.7 GiB available, 67 GB root free. Existing Cloudflare tunnel has no Campsite routes.
- Shuri: M1 16 GB, about 100 GiB disk free. Shadow Elasticsearch is green, capped at 2 GiB with a 1 GiB heap, using about 1.36 GiB.
- Forge: halted, 4 GiB/4 vCPU, auto_poweron false. It cannot be treated as an always-available build path until deliberately started/configured.
- Odin, Heimdall, Hermes, and Plex have auto_poweron true.
- starkdrive: 3.6 TB total, 730 GB free, 81 percent used.
- Existing XO VM backups are present, but no Campsite-specific database, object, or Elasticsearch backups were found. The current Shuri Elasticsearch is outside XCP-ng VM backup coverage.
- No UPS evidence was found. Treat the platform as single-site and power-loss exposed.

WORKING SERVICE CONSTRAINTS for this 1-2 user deployment, pending any later operator override:
- RPO: at most 24 hours for durable application data at initial cutover; Redis cache is disposable, but Sidekiq durable jobs require drain/reconciliation.
- RTO: at most 8 hours.
- Planned cutover maintenance window: at most 4 hours.
- Rollback window: retain old production read-only or switchable for 7 days.
- No public database, Redis, Elasticsearch, or object-storage administration ports.
- Backups must be restored in rehearsal before cutover; presence alone is not acceptance.

AUDIT CONCLUSION:
Every production component and data source has an identified owner/path. Live data quantities requiring Fly/provider authority are explicitly UNAVAILABLE. Odin is suitable for low-traffic stateless runtimes; Shuri is suitable for capped single-node Elasticsearch. The platform design must account for Asgard host memory pressure, Forge availability, Shuri backup coverage, single-site power risk, and starkdrive capacity.
close_reason: Live topology, data ownership, capacity, and recovery constraints audited; inaccessible provider metrics explicitly marked unavailable.

Preserve the existing camp*.polo-apps.com deployment until the new stack passes external, authenticated, provider, backup/restore, and human UAT gates.

Make production hostnames environment-configurable so old and new stacks can coexist. Use restore-based rehearsals and an explicit write-quiescence window for final database/object cutover. Never run old and new Sidekiq schedulers concurrently. Do not redirect API/webhook/WebSocket endpoints during the rollback window.
